name: Graph model and GLSL generator
body:
A material graph is an ordinary graph file whose single function is `material` and whose nodes are `mat_` kinds, so the graph canvas, file format and editing are reused. `lantern:::materialgraph:::GenerateMaterialShader(graph)` turns it into a GLSL `SurfaceOf` function that the lit fragment shader calls instead of reading the uniform material.

Nodes: `mat_scalar`, `mat_color`, `mat_param` (a Silhouette value, baked in as a constant), `mat_texture` (sample a texture by UV, up to four per material), `mat_uv`, `mat_add`, `mat_mul`, `mat_lerp`, `mat_one_minus`, `mat_clamp`, and one `mat_output` with base colour, metallic, roughness, emissive and normal (a tangent-space normal, e.g. a normal-map texture sample).

The generator's test checks the generated text and the refusals, naming the node at fault. The bake (the bake feature) compiles each generated shader with glslangValidator and spirv-cross, so a graph the generator accepts but GLSL refuses stops the bake with the compiler's message.
